#### 1. long QT syndrome 6  —  Tier 2 — Strong / Probable  (fitness 0.654)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:6242)

**Proposed mechanism:** KCNE2 (HGNC:6242) —BINDS→ KCNQ1 (HGNC:6241); KCNQ1 (HGNC:6241) —LEADS_TO→ Potassium channel activity; KCNE2 (HGNC:6242) —DISRUPTS→ Potassium channel activity; Potassium channel activity —LEADS_TO→ Congenital long QT syndrome (HP:0011675); Potassium channel activity —LEADS_TO→ Atrial standstill (HP:0005175). Mutations in KCNE2 lead to haploinsufficiency, impairing the function of the KCNQ1/KCNE2 potassium channel complex. This disruption in potassium channel activity results in prolonged cardiac repolarization, manifesting as congenital long QT syndrome (MONDO:0013370), and can also lead to atrial standstill (MONDO:0012677).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in KCNE2 that are exclusively associated with one disease phenotype and not the other, or the discovery of distinct molecular mechanisms for each disease not involving KCNE2, would falsify this hypothesis.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared KCNE2 mechanism offers opportunities for unified therapeutic strategies targeting potassium channel function for both congenital long QT syndrome and atrial standstill, potentially improving patient outcomes.
